Job description: Director of Development
Caldsted Foundation has welcomed seniors of modest means into a warm, compassionate community since 1965.  Today, more than fifty residents live independently in a supportive and gracious community that provides comfortable housing, meals, housekeeping, and transportation.  Our mission is to provide seniors with limited resources, housing and services that preserve their independence and promote healthy living with dignity.
We are seeking to hire a Development Associate (DA) to ensure the longevity of the Caldsted Foundation (Caldsted) by supporting the implementation of Caldsted’s fundraising strategy around unrestricted donations and grant funding.  The DA will report to the Executive Director (ED) and will work with the foundation staff and board of directors.  You will be responsible for planning and implementing strategies to secure individual and organizational investment in the key elements of Caldsted’s mission offerings and general support of the organization, oversee the business and donor fund development program, monitor development activities, and address issues that may hamper growth and success.
The successful applicant should have proven experience in business development, with experience in a non-profit organization or a similar environment (though not required).  You must be a motivated self-starter, with the ability to foster strong partnerships, and have a passion for philanthropy.
Responsibilities:
In collaboration with the ED and Board, develop and implement a strategic plan for single and multi-year resource development efforts:
Provide support in positioning the Board to cultivate and solicit major gifts and grants from individuals, foundations, corporations, United Way, government agencies and others;
Research and analyze individual, corporate, agency, and foundation donor base and recommend solicitation strategies;
Develop relationships with industry thought leaders and influencers with the objective of enhancing Caldsted’s reputation as an expert in independent, senior living communities.
Write and submit grant proposals that demonstrate a compelling need for financial support in the 5-7 figure range;
Cultivate relationships with Board members and provide tools to Board to serve as effective fundraisers, including prospect research and written materials, as well as the cultivation of new funder leads;
Oversee planning and preparation of related printed materials, publications, and solicitation materials;
Maintain annual fundraising tracking database, donation files, and gift requests, as well as create and maintain a donor record database with notes and background information as known to ensure information is institutionalized;
Serve as relationship holder for donors;
Identify opportunities for increases from existing donors;
Oversee evaluation of development activities and identify opportunities to improve results; and
Provide support for various fundraising strategies/projects/initiatives that may be assigned by the ED and/or Board, such as endowments, major gifts, planned giving, and event planning.
Provide leadership to staff in support of resource development.
Keep abreast of developments in targeted corporate, government, and education markets.
Desired Outcomes:
·       Assimilate effectively into Caldsted’s culture and develop a strong understanding of our mission.
·       Serve as a key contributor in planning Caldsted’s growth and value creation and in developing a strategy to build Caldsted’s current capabilities and plans.
·       Partner with Caldsted’s staff, board of directors, third-party providers, industry experts and partners to catapult our impact to the next level of financial growth by developing and executing an effective development plan.
Desired Attributes:
Bachelor’s degree preferred in nonprofit management, business administration, marketing, communications, or related field
Minimum of 2 years of professional experience (experience in sales, client development, funder relationship management and/or grant writing preferred)
Experience and/or comfort with business development, client development and/or fundraising
Strong interpersonal, decision-making, and leadership skills
Analytical thinking and ability to analyze data
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Exceptional organization and project management skills
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, Board members and volunteers
Commitment to the mission, vision, values and guiding principles of Caldsted
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other computer software, along with electronic communication mediums including online fundraising, website updates and social media messaging
Occasional local travel required
Interested candidates may submit a resume and cover letter to:  Joanna King at jking@caldsted.com for consideration.

Join the City of Chattanooga Team Chattanooga , a vibrant and growing community of over 190,000 residents within a metropolitan area of nearly 600,000 is known as the "Scenic City" for a reason. Our team ensures our city thrives through a wide range of municipal services, including: Public Safety: Chattanooga Police and Fire Departments. Infrastructure Utilities: Public Works, Waste Resources, and specialized Stormwater management. Quality of Life: Award-winning Parks and Outdoors and Community Development systems and the Chattanooga Public Library. Transportation: The Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and citywide transit and pedestrian friendly initiatives. Innovation: Leading-edge smart-city programs with a commitment to cutting edge workforce development policies to ensure all our residents can get ahead. Why Choose Chattanooga? Work-Life Balance: Generous paid time off and flexible scheduling where possible. Exceptional Wellness: Comprehensive health benefits and wellness programs designed for you and your family that deliver savings to you beyond your paycheck, featuring a centralized health clinic and pharmacy for all City employees. . Growth: A focus on professional development and upward mobility within the organization. ​The Great Outdoors: Your Backyard Playground: Chattanooga isn't just near nature, it's immersed in it. As one of the most biodiverse cities in North America, the "Scenic City" offers an ecological richness that few places on earth can claim. Whether you are an adrenaline junkie or a weekend wanderer, world-class adventure is always less than an hour away. ​Vertical Adventures: Scale legendary sandstone cliffs in what is widely considered the premier rock climbing hub of the Southeast. Water Rapids: From the high-octane whitewater kayaking of the Ocoee River to world-class bass fishing and peaceful paddling on the Tennessee River. Trails for Miles: Explore a massive network of mountain biking and hiking trails that wind through lush ridges, hidden waterfalls, and deep river gorges. Help Build a Stronger Future for Children, Youth, and Families
Do you enjoy building relationships, connecting people to meaningful causes, and turning ideas into action? Are you organized, detail-oriented, and motivated by making a difference in your community? Chambliss Center for Children is seeking a passionate and driven Development Coordinator to support fundraising events, donor engagement, grant development, community partnerships, and stewardship activities. This is an exciting opportunity for a development professional who enjoys both relationship building and event planning while helping create life-changing opportunities for children, youth, and families throughout our community.
About Chambliss Center for Children
For more than 150 years, Chambliss Center for Children has been helping children, youth, and families build brighter futures. Chambliss provides a wide range of services that strengthen families and create opportunities for young people to thrive, including:

Early childhood education and childcare programs for infants through school-age children
Foster care placement and support services in partnership with the State of Tennessee
Adoption services that help children find safe, permanent homes
A Transitional Living Program that provides housing, life skills training, and support for young adults aging out of foster care
Innovative “micro-centers” located within Hamilton County schools that provide convenient, high-quality onsite childcare for teachers and school employees.

Every day, Chambliss helps working families access reliable childcare, supports children in foster care, assists youth transitioning to independence, and creates stronger outcomes for the entire community. When you join Chambliss, your work directly supports programs that impact children and families across the Chattanooga region. Every donor relationship, grant award, sponsorship, and fundraising event helps expand opportunities for those who need them most.
What You’ll Do

Assist in coordinating fundraising events from planning through execution
Research grant opportunities and assist with grant writing and reporting
Maintain grant calendars, deadlines, and support documentation
Serve as a point of contact for third-party fundraising partners
Manage and grow the monthly giving program
Prepare donor acknowledgments, impact reports, and donor communications
Maintain accurate donor and gift records in the donor database
Represent Chambliss Center at community events, networking opportunities, and tours
Build positive relationships with donors, volunteers, sponsors, and community partners

What We’re Looking For
We’re seeking a mission-driven professional who combines strong organizational skills with a passion for relationship building.
Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in communications, marketing, nonprofit management, public relations, business, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
Experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, donor relations, marketing, communications, or event planning
Grant writing and/or grant research experience preferred
Experience coordinating projects with multiple deadlines and stakeholders
Experience using donor databases (CRM systems) and fundraising software
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications

Key Qualities for Success

Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong attention to detail and project management abilities
Relationship-focused with a genuine passion for connecting with people
Self-motivated and able to work independently
Curious, resourceful, and skilled at researching opportunities
Flexible and adaptable in a fast-paced environment
Professional, dependable, and trustworthy
Passionate about helping children and strengthening communities

Under Jessica's leadership, NNH has continued the work we've done for more than 100 years, uplifting and empowering our neighbors north of the river. Organization Overview: For more than 100 years, Northside Neighborhood House (NNH) has existed to uplift and empower our neighbors north of the river. Our footprint is northern Hamilton County, and we are intentionally rooted there, staying proximate to the neighbors we serve rather than spreading thin. Within that footprint, NNH has grown tremendously over the last twenty years: a tenfold operating budget increase, new innovative programming, two sites to five, and 13 employees in 2006 to more than 70 today.

Stability Program: Case management, financial assistance, and empowerment programming that moves neighbors from crisis to long-term stability.
Community Schools: Coordinators in ten area schools supporting students, families, and the whole school community.
Thrift Stores: Three stores offering low-cost clothing, furniture, and household items while helping fund the mission.

 
Role Summary: The CEO reports to the Board of Directors and leads NNH strategically, operationally, and fiscally. This is both an outward-facing and an inward-facing role: cultivating the funding and the people NNH needs, guiding the strategic plan, partnering closely with an engaged board, and building a workplace where a strong team can do its best work. This role leads the whole organization; it does not run programs day to day.
The right person leads with relationships, is at ease asking for support, and keeps NNH accountable to the neighbors it serves. If you can hold vision and follow-through in the same hand, this is your team.
 
Job Responsibilities:

Strategic vision & leadership: Refine and implement the strategic plan with the Board and Leadership Team; lead long-range planning for facilities and locations so the agency stays proximate to our neighbors.
Finance: Partner with the CFO on the annual budget and monthly reporting; set financial priorities that support programming and staff.
Fundraising & community engagement: Cultivate the funding NNH needs, carry a portfolio of major donor relationships, serve as spokesperson, and equip the board in its fundraising role.
Board governance & partnership: Serve as primary liaison to the Board; support recruitment, onboarding, and development; partner with the Board Chair on meaningful agendas.
Infrastructure & operations: Ensure high-quality services while managing for growth; build an engaged, inclusive work environment through strong internal communication.
Data, outcomes & improvement: Own agency outcomes and report quarterly to the board, using data to drive decisions and share NNH’s impact.

 
Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required
Ten+ years progressive experience, incl. five in senior leadership
Fundraising, board development, marketing, and fiscal management
Nonprofit multi-site experience preferred; comparable private-sector executives equally considered
Experience with volunteers is ideal

 
Employee Benefits

PTO, holiday pay & paid parental leave
Employer-supported health insurance
Dental & vision plans available
Long-term disability & life insurance
TextCare

Within SWORPS, the Tennessee Child Support Employment and Parenting Program (TCSEPP) Coordinator builds a strong evidence-informed and trauma-informed practice that assists, supports, and advocates for non-custodial parents involved with the child support system. The TCSEPP Coordinator, based in HAMILTON COUNTY, TN, assists non-custodial parents with overcoming barriers to employment in order to become stable, obtain employment, pay child support, become self-sufficient, and be an active parent in their child(ren)’s lives. The Coordinator works with non-custodial parents to promote trust and communication between them and the systems with which they interact as well as with, when possible and appropriate, with the children and custodial parents.  The Coordinator also weaves together a supportive network of formal and informal community-based resources for non-custodial parents and provides outreach and education to non-custodial parents and the community-at-large.
Responsibilities
Determine participant eligibility and properly assess participants’ barriers and make appropriate referrals for identified barriers 
Develop individual action plans for participants and provide one-on-one case management to participants to assist them with job readiness activities and emotional support and encouragement 
Maintain accurate records of all participant interactions in appropriate places, i.e. TCSES, Apricot, Excel spreadsheet, etc. 
Monitor participants’ child support eligibility & payments; program involvement & compliance as well as employment.
Develop and maintain partnerships with local agencies to assist participants with barriers to employment 
Attend community interagency meetings to learn about and share available resources and information 
Participate in partner meetings 
Provide regular updates to Child Support staff and attorneys on participant progress 
Maintain a court presence to foster a positive relationship with the Child Support legal system and to recruit and/or enroll potential participants 
Participate in job/resource fairs 
Fiscal tasks including but not limited to One Card reconciliation and uploading & documenting receipts, monthly gift card reconciliation, and travel reports

Must have valid driver’s license, automobile at their disposal, and a current automobile liability policy with continuous coverage.
Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:
Ability to assess participant needs.
Ability to develop positive & trusting relationships with participants and offer emotional support.
Ability to positively interact with partners including child support, court, attorneys, etc.
Ability to promote the program to potential participants, partners, and employers.
Ability to advocate for participants.
Ability to work independently and within a team setting.
Ability to travel to multiple counties to serve participants.
Ability to be flexible with respect to changing needs of the project.
Excellent oral communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
Ability to work independently and in team settings.
Experience with data management systems.
